**Clinical Note Template**

**1. Patient Information**

Name: Arthur Miller
Age/Gender: 80/Male
Hospital Stay Dates: October 26, 2023 to November 15, 2023 (with multiple admissions/discharges within this period)
Admitting Diagnosis:  Suspected colorectal cancer with obstructive symptoms
Discharge Diagnosis: Stage II Colon Cancer,  Dehydration,  Hypokalemia,  Post-operative ileus


**2. Visit Details**

**[October 26, 2023, 14:30]**

Provider Role: Emergency Physician
Reason for Visit:  Severe abdominal pain, constipation, nausea, vomiting for 3 days.
Interventions:  Complete blood count (CBC), comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP), abdominal X-ray, CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis.
Findings/Results:  CBC showed mild leukocytosis (WBC 12.5 x 10^9/L). CMP revealed hypokalemia (K+ 3.0 mmol/L) and dehydration. Abdominal X-ray showed significant colonic distension. CT scan showed a large, obstructing mass in the sigmoid colon with evidence of bowel wall thickening and adjacent lymphadenopathy.
Treatment Plan:  Intravenous fluids (normal saline), potassium supplementation, nasogastric tube placement for decompression, bowel rest, and admission to the surgical service for further evaluation and potential surgical intervention.


**[October 27, 2023, 09:00]**

Provider Role: Surgical Oncology Fellow
Reason for Visit:  Assessment and planning for surgical intervention.
Interventions:  Review of imaging studies, physical examination.
Findings/Results:  Patient remains symptomatic despite nasogastric decompression.  Physical exam reveals significant abdominal distension and tenderness.
Treatment Plan:  Scheduled for emergency sigmoid colectomy with possible temporary colostomy.


**[October 27, 2023, 15:00]**

Provider Role: Surgeon
Reason for Visit:  Emergency sigmoid colectomy.
Interventions:  Sigmoid colectomy with end colostomy.  Intraoperative findings consistent with CT scan.  Biopsy specimens sent for pathology.
Findings/Results:  Surgery completed without major complications.  Patient transferred to post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) in stable condition.


**[October 28, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role: Surgical Attending
Reason for Visit:  Post-operative assessment.
Interventions:  Physical examination, review of post-operative labs.
Findings/Results:  Patient is alert and oriented, but complaining of mild abdominal discomfort.  Bowel sounds are hypoactive.  Incisional site is clean and dry.  Post-operative labs show improving electrolyte levels.
Treatment Plan:  Continue intravenous fluids, pain management with morphine sulfate PCA pump, and bowel rest.  Monitor for signs of infection or complications.


**[October 30, 2023, 11:00]**

Provider Role: Surgical Attending
Reason for Visit:  Persistent post-operative ileus.
Interventions:  Abdominal examination, repeat abdominal X-ray.
Findings/Results:  Abdominal X-ray shows persistent air-fluid levels, consistent with ileus.  Patient continues to report abdominal discomfort.
Treatment Plan:  Continue bowel rest, increase intravenous fluids, and initiate metoclopramide for gastrointestinal motility.


**[November 2, 2023, 14:00]**

Provider Role: Surgical Attending
Reason for Visit:  Follow-up on post-operative ileus.
Interventions:  Physical exam, abdominal exam.
Findings/Results:  Significant improvement in abdominal distension and discomfort.  Bowel sounds are now audible.
Treatment Plan:  Discontinue metoclopramide.  Advance diet as tolerated.  Plan for discharge in the next 2 days.


**[November 5, 2023, 09:00]**

Provider Role:  Medical Oncologist
Reason for Visit:  Pathology report review and oncology consultation.
Interventions:  Review of pathology report.
Findings/Results:  Pathology confirmed moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the sigmoid colon (Stage II).
Treatment Plan:  Recommend adjuvant chemotherapy following recovery from surgery.  Referral to oncology clinic for further planning.


**[November 7, 2023, 16:00]**

Provider Role:  Surgical Attending
Reason for Visit:  Discharge planning.
Interventions:  Wound assessment, patient education.
Findings/Results:  Wound healing well.  Patient education regarding colostomy care provided.
Treatment Plan:  Discharge planned for tomorrow.


**[November 8, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role:  Surgical Attending
Reason for Visit:  Discharge.
Interventions:  Final physical exam, discharge instructions given.
Findings/Results:  Patient stable for discharge.
Treatment Plan:  Discharged to home with instructions for wound care and colostomy care.


**3. Key Events During Hospitalization**

* Emergency sigmoid colectomy performed on October 27, 2023.
* Post-operative ileus developed, resolving by November 2, 2023.
* Pathology confirmed Stage II colon cancer on November 5, 2023.


**4. Ongoing Management and Care**

Intravenous fluids, potassium supplementation, nasogastric tube placement, pain management with morphine sulfate PCA pump, metoclopramide,  antibiotics (prophylactically), wound care.


**5. Discharge Summary**

Discharge Medications:  Colace (stool softener),  Docusate sodium (stool softener),  Acetaminophen (pain relief),  Multivitamin.
Follow-up Instructions:  Follow up appointment with surgical oncology in 2 weeks.  Follow-up appointment with medical oncology in 1 week to discuss chemotherapy options.  Colostomy nurse follow-up scheduled for next week.
Prognosis:  Guarded.  Prognosis is dependent on response to adjuvant chemotherapy.  Long-term survival is expected with appropriate treatment.

**[November 15, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role:  Medical Oncologist
Reason for Visit:  Initial consultation to discuss adjuvant chemotherapy plan.
Interventions:  Review of pathology report, discussion of treatment options, assessment of patient's overall health and fitness for chemotherapy.
Findings/Results:  Patient is recovering well from surgery.  He is alert and oriented, and his wound is healing well.  Discussion included FOLFOX regimen versus CAPOX regimen, considering his age and overall health.  Patient expresses concerns about side effects.
Treatment Plan:  Initiate FOLFOX regimen (oxaliplatin, leucovorin, and 5-fluorouracil) starting next week.  Schedule blood work prior to first cycle.  Prescribe antiemetic medication (Ondansetron) to manage nausea.  Patient education provided regarding chemotherapy side effects and management strategies.  Scheduled follow-up appointment in one week to monitor for adverse effects.

**[November 22, 2023, 14:30]**

Provider Role: Surgical Oncology Fellow
Reason for Visit:  Follow-up appointment post-discharge.  Assessment of wound healing and colostomy function.
Interventions:  Physical examination of the surgical site, assessment of the colostomy, review of patient's home wound care practices.  Patient reports some mild discomfort around the stoma.
Findings/Results:  Wound healing is progressing well.  Minimal serosanguinous drainage noted.  Colostomy is functioning adequately, with regular output.  Patient demonstrates good understanding of colostomy care.  Mild erythema noted around the stoma, likely due to irritation from the appliance.
Treatment Plan:  Recommend alternative ostomy appliance to minimize irritation.  Prescribe topical hydrocortisone cream for erythema.  Schedule follow-up appointment in one week.  Reinforce wound care instructions.

**[November 29, 2023, 11:00]**

Provider Role: Medical Oncologist
Reason for Visit:  Follow-up after first cycle of FOLFOX chemotherapy.
Interventions:  Review of complete blood count (CBC), comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP), and assessment of treatment-related side effects.  Patient reports experiencing nausea and fatigue.
Findings/Results:  CBC shows mild neutropenia (absolute neutrophil count 1.2 x 10^9/L).  CMP is within normal limits.  Patient reports moderate nausea and fatigue, managed with Ondansetron.  No other significant side effects reported.
Treatment Plan:  Continue FOLFOX regimen, but decrease dose of oxaliplatin by 25% for the next cycle due to neutropenia.  Increase dose of Ondansetron to manage nausea.  Recommend increased rest and hydration.  Schedule blood work before the next cycle.  Closely monitor for signs of infection due to neutropenia.  Schedule a follow-up appointment in one week.

**3. Key Events During Hospitalization** *(Existing entry,  needs updating)*

* Emergency sigmoid colectomy performed on October 27, 2023.
* Post-operative ileus developed, resolving by November 2, 2023.
* Pathology confirmed Stage II colon cancer on November 5, 2023.
* Adjuvant FOLFOX chemotherapy initiated on November 22, 2023.

**4. Ongoing Management and Care** *(Existing entry, needs updating)*

Intravenous fluids (during hospitalization), potassium supplementation (during hospitalization), nasogastric tube placement (during hospitalization), pain management with morphine sulfate PCA pump (during hospitalization), metoclopramide (during hospitalization),  antibiotics (prophylactically, during hospitalization), wound care, Colace, Docusate sodium, Acetaminophen, Multivitamin, Ondansetron, topical hydrocortisone cream, FOLFOX chemotherapy.


**5. Discharge Summary** *(Existing entry, needs updating)*

Discharge Medications:  Colace (stool softener),  Docusate sodium (stool softener),  Acetaminophen (pain relief),  Multivitamin, Ondansetron (antiemetic), topical hydrocortisone cream.
Follow-up Instructions:  Follow up appointment with surgical oncology as needed.  Follow-up appointment with medical oncology weekly during chemotherapy cycles.  Colostomy nurse follow-up as needed.
Prognosis:  Guarded.  Prognosis is dependent on response to adjuvant chemotherapy.  Long-term survival is expected with appropriate treatment.  Close monitoring for chemotherapy-related side effects is crucial.

Provider Role:  Medical Oncology Nurse Practitioner
Reason for Visit:  Follow-up after discharge; initiation of chemotherapy regimen.
Interventions:  Physical examination, review of discharge medications, blood work (CBC, CMP, LFTs). Patient education regarding chemotherapy side effects and management.
Findings/Results:  Patient reports mild fatigue and occasional nausea.  Physical examination reveals well-healing surgical incision.  CBC shows mild anemia (Hgb 10.8 g/dL). CMP and LFTs within normal limits.
Treatment Plan:  Initiate FOLFOX chemotherapy regimen.  Prescribe Ondansetron for nausea.  Schedule weekly blood counts to monitor for hematologic toxicity.  Encourage increased fluid intake and high-protein diet.  Advised patient to report any significant side effects immediately.

**[November 22, 2023, 14:30]**

Provider Role: Medical Oncologist
Reason for Visit:  First cycle FOLFOX chemotherapy follow-up.
Interventions:  Review of blood work (CBC, CMP), assessment of chemotherapy side effects, physical examination.
Findings/Results:  Patient reports increased fatigue and mild diarrhea.  CBC shows mild leukopenia (WBC 3.8 x 10^9/L) but otherwise within acceptable limits for post-chemotherapy. CMP within normal limits. Patient reports good response to Ondansetron.
Treatment Plan:  Continue FOLFOX regimen, adjust dose of Ondansetron to manage diarrhea.  Schedule blood work next week to monitor for further hematologic suppression.  Recommend increasing hydration and fiber intake.  Discuss management of fatigue, including rest periods and energy conservation strategies.

Provider Role:  Surgical Oncology Fellow
Reason for Visit:  Follow-up on surgical site and colostomy.
Interventions:  Wound assessment, colostomy assessment, patient education.

Treatment Plan:  Reinforce colostomy care instructions.  Schedule a follow up with the colostomy nurse next week.  Arrange for a home health nurse visit to provide additional support with colostomy care.  Continue to monitor for any signs of infection or complications at the surgical site.
